issue.title: Defer workspace claim release out of the SIGTERM handler
issue.description: The SIGTERM callback in install_workspace_release_sigterm_handler calls release_workspace and clear_occupant_record synchronously. release_workspace enters patch_lock(project_file), whose flock retry loop has a 30-second timeout. Repro: deliver SIGTERM while the runner main thread holds the same project patch lock; the Python handler re-enters release_workspace and cannot return to let the original lock scope unwind, so it waits for the timeout. The callback then clears the occupant record even if release_workspace failed, while the RUNNING claim may remain. Move claim release to normal runner control flow while preserving prompt release and handoff behavior.

task_type_fields.impact: An agent kill can stall shutdown for up to the workspace lock timeout and leave the RUNNING claim inconsistent with the cleared occupant marker.
task_type_fields.repro: Deliver SIGTERM while the runner main thread holds patch_lock(project_file); observe the synchronous signal callback re-enter release_workspace and wait for the lock timeout before the original critical section can unwind.

issue.creation_reason: While implementing the approved SIGTERM fix, I verified that the runner’s signal callback still performs file-locked workspace release. This separate path can delay shutdown and leave the workspace claim and occupant record out of sync.
